question: If the power of a lens is +1 Dioptre, then the focal length of the lens will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**+1 Dioptre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power of a lens (P) in dioptres is the reciprocal of the focal length (f) in meters, represented as P = 1/f.
 
• If the power of the lens is +1 Dioptre, the focal length (f) can be calculated using the formula: f = 1/P.
 
• Substituting the given power, f = 1/1 = 1 meter.
 
• A positive dioptre value indicates that the lens is a converging lens, typically used for correcting hyperopia (farsightedness).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dioptre (D):** A unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens, defined as the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (1/m).
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the lens and the point where parallel rays of light converge (for a converging lens) or appear to diverge (for a diverging lens).
 
• **Converging Lens:** Also known as a convex lens, it bends light rays inward, bringing them to a focus. Used in applications like magnifying glasses and corrective lenses for hyperopia.
 
• **Diverging Lens:** Also known as a concave lens, it spreads out light rays that have been refracted through it. Used in applications like corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).
 
• **Hyperopia (Farsightedness):** A condition where distant objects are seen more clearly than near ones. Converging lenses with positive dioptre values are used for correction.
